events.title: Nat Turner's Rebellion Begins in Virginia
events.description: Late on the night of August 21, Nat Turner, an enslaved preacher, led a group of enslaved people in an uprising in Southampton County, Virginia. Over the next day or so they moved from farm to farm. The revolt was put down within days.
events.significance: It was one of the most significant slave uprisings in US history. It triggered harsh repression and led Southern states to tighten laws on enslaved and free Black people.

events.title: The Mona Lisa Is Stolen from the Louvre
events.description: Leonardo da Vinci's Mona Lisa was taken from the Louvre in Paris. The theft was carried out by a former museum worker, Vincenzo Peruggia. The painting stayed missing for more than two years before it was recovered in Italy.
events.significance: The theft made headlines around the world and turned a respected artwork into a global celebrity. Many historians credit it with launching the painting's modern fame.

events.title: Hawaii Becomes the 50th US State
events.description: President Dwight D. Eisenhower formally proclaimed Hawaii's admission to the Union, which made it the 50th state. The proclamation followed a statehood vote by Hawaii's residents and approval by Congress earlier that year.
events.significance: Hawaii was the last state to join the Union. It was also the first with a majority Asian American and Pacific Islander population.

events.title: The August Coup Collapses in the Soviet Union
events.description: A coup against Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev, mounted by hardline Communist officials, failed after about three days. Mass public resistance in Moscow, led by Boris Yeltsin, helped bring it down.
events.significance: The failed coup discredited the Communist hardliners and sped up the Soviet Union's breakup. The USSR dissolved a few months later, in December 1991.
